prompt:
A grand establishing landscape on a clear, bright morning: the sunward face of the dwarven mountains, the most beautifully made place in the world. Homes and gate share one architecture: plain stone, clean horizontal lines, bold cantilevers, gardens on every roof.

Setting: the whole sunward face of a great mountain, seen from across the valley. The homes are hundreds of plain rectangular stone blocks stacked and offset up the slope in the spirit of Habitat 67: each block shifted from the one below so that every roof is the planted garden terrace of the home above, blocks bridging and cantilevering over each other at different angles, open-air walkways and stairs threading between them, bands of glass windows; a dense, interlocking, three-dimensional hillside of homes carved from and built onto the living rock. Below and between them, tier after tier of green barley terraces cascade down the slope. In the centre a huge waterfall pours out of the rock, and the great gate is ONE great building built over and into it: long, wide horizontal stone floors cantilevered right across the falling water like Fallingwater made monumental, in exactly the same clean style as the homes. Stone channels carry water from the falls across the terraces and turn the waterwheels of forges, whose smoke rises from neat openings in the cliff. The river runs on down the valley through pine forest toward the distant lowlands; snow-capped peaks above.

The dwarven mountains look: an alpine range of grey stone, dark pine forest and snow-capped peaks at the headwaters of a river. Dwarven architecture is beauty without ornament, in the spirit of Frank Lloyd Wright and Mies van der Rohe: long, clean horizontal slabs of stone cantilevered out of the living rock over open air, deep overhangs, bands of windows, crisp right angles, every surface plain and perfectly made; it is beautiful because it works, never because it is decorated.

Palette: pale grey granite, warm honey-coloured stone, the green of planted terraces, white water, snow and dark pine.

Do not draw: boxy whitewashed hill-town cubes, thin walkways in place of the gate, pueblo adobe, carved ornament, runes, gold trim, giant statues, fantasy dwarf halls with pillars and braziers, grim iron doors, organic curves or Gaudí shapes.

Style: Sword-and-sorcery comic art in the spirit of 1970s-80s Conan the Barbarian and Masters of the Universe: bold confident ink outlines, dramatic lighting, saturated flat colours with hard cel shading and halftone-dot shading, pulpy and dramatic. No text, no logos, no speech bubbles.

Composition: a tight crop from the middle of a larger illustration, so the artwork runs off all four edges of the image. Nothing surrounds the art: no border, no white or cream margin, no paper, no frame, no panel outline.

Show only what is described. If no people or creatures are mentioned, the scene is empty of them: no figures, silhouettes or onlookers.
